newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Goodman says preparing fresh Defiance bid.
newsitem.headline: Goodman says preparing fresh Defiance bid.

text.p: Goodman Fielder Ltd said on Wednesday it was preparing a revised proposal for the New Zealand Commerce Commission following the rejection of its proposed takeover of the NZ milling and baking assets of Defiance Mills Ltd.
Goodman Fielder chief executive David Hearn said the bid would accommodate the concerns of the Commerce Commission in areas it had identified earlier this week.

"Our primary objective is to develop a proposal that is acceptable to all parties, including the regulatory authorities, and suppliers and customers in New Zealand, as quickly as possible to end uncertainty for shareholders and staff," Hearn said in a statement.
The Commission on Monday declined to clear the NZ$48 million purchase because of concerns Goodman Fielder could acquire or strengthen a dominant position in a number of markets.
Competition concerns included high barriers to new entry, a lack of competition, high market share and a lack of constraint on Goodman Fielder from both suppliers and purchasers.
Both Goodman Fielder and Defiance Mills are based in Australia and have extensive interests in New Zealand.
Goodman announced the proposed purchase in March, saying it would consolidate its market position in New Zealand.
